# Clinic Appointment Visualization Plan

A simple two-chart setup will show both the **time burden** of visits and the **kind of outcomes** patients receive. This works well for a non-technical audience because it separates “how long people waited” from “what happened next.”

## Recommended Charts and What They Reveal

| Chart | Best Chart Type | What It Reveals | Why It Helps |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wait time by age group and visit reason | Grouped bar chart | Which age/reason combinations have the longest waits | Makes delays easy to compare across patient groups |
| Visit outcome by age group and visit reason | Stacked bar chart or heatmap | Which outcomes are most common for each group | Shows whether certain visits tend to end in referral, resolution, or medication changes |

### Chart 1: Wait Time by Age Group and Visit Reason
- Plot **age group** on the x-axis and **wait time minutes** on the y-axis.
- Use color to separate **visit reason**.
- This will quickly show that:
  - **65+ chronic care** has the longest wait in the dataset at **35 minutes**
  - **65+ follow-up** is also high at **31 minutes**
  - Shorter waits appear in **preventive visits** for **30-44 (14 minutes)** and **45-64 (16 minutes)**

### Chart 2: Visit Outcome by Age Group and Visit Reason
- Use a **stacked bar chart** if you want a simple count view, or a **heatmap** if you want a cleaner “pattern map.”
- This will show that:
  - **Resolved** outcomes are common in **follow-up** and **preventive** visits
  - **Referred** outcomes appear in **new issue** visits for **18-29** and **30-44**
  - **Medication adjusted** appears in the **65+** group for **chronic care** and **follow-up**

## Notable Patterns for a Non-Technical Audience

- **Older patients wait longer in this dataset.** The two longest waits are both in the **65+** group.
- **Preventive visits seem to move faster.** Both preventive rows have relatively low wait times and end in **resolved** outcomes.
- **New issues are more likely to be referred.** That suggests these visits may need additional evaluation or follow-up care.
- **Follow-up visits often end positively.** In this dataset, follow-ups are split between **resolved** and **medication adjusted**, which suggests they are often used to confirm progress or fine-tune treatment.

## Quick Actions
